definition.description: The anatomical location of brain metastases within the cerebral lobes.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the specific cerebral lobe(s) where brain metastases are identified in the pretreatment imaging or clinical reports (e.g., Occipital, Parietal, Frontal, Temporal).
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain metastases are documented or if the specific lobe location is not mentioned.
definition.name: brain_metastases_location

definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether brain metastases (intracranial lesions) are present or absent based on radiographic evidence (e.g., brain MRI, CT) or clinical documentation in the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the record contains no information, explicitly states the status is unknown or uncertain, or if imaging was inconclusive due to technical limitations.
definition.name: brain_metastases_presence

definition.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in brain structures.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record reports 'abnormal enhancement' or 'contrast enhancement' within brain structures (e.g., brainstem, cerebellum, or ventricles).
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no mention of abnormal enhancement or if the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: brain_structure_enhancement

definition.description: Assessment of the radiologic signal intensity of the brainstem on MRI.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the reported signal appearance of the brainstem from neuroimaging reports; 'normal', 'unremarkable', or 'no abnormal signal' should be mapped to Normal, while any mention of abnormal signal intensity, lesions, or pathology within the brainstem should be mapped to Abnormal.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the brainstem signal is not explicitly mentioned or if the documentation is too ambiguous to categorize.
definition.name: brainstem_signal

definition.description: Qualitative assessment of the brainstem size based on neuroimaging.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the reported size of the brainstem from neuroimaging (e.g., MRI, CT). If the report states the brainstem is 'normal in size', 'unremarkable', or 'within normal limits', record as 'Normal'. If the report indicates atrophy, enlargement, or any other size-related abnormality, record as 'Abnormal'.
definition.missing_value_rule: If the brainstem size is not mentioned or cannot be determined from the text, return null.
definition.name: brainstem_size

definition.description: The total daily energy intake of the patient described qualitatively.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the qualitative descriptor of the total daily caloric intake, such as 'low', 'adequate', or 'high'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent missing or ambiguous documentation as null.
definition.name: calorie_intake

definition.description: Presence of lytic or sclerotic lesions in the calvarium.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether lytic or sclerotic lesions are reported to be present or absent in the calvarium (skull) from imaging reports.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the calvarium is not mentioned or if the report is ambiguous regarding the presence of these lesions.
definition.name: calvarium_lytic_sclerotic_lesions

definition.description: Whether the patient has a documented diagnosis of cancer.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract 'Yes' if the medical record contains a diagnosis of malignancy or cancer; otherwise extract 'No'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if no mention of cancer is found or if the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: cancer_diagnosis

definition.description: The anatomical location of the patient's cancer.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the anatomical site or organ identified as the location of the carcinoma or adenocarcinoma from the pretreatment medical records.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no location is specified or documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: cancer_location

definition.description: The severity of cancer-related fatigue as measured by the PRO-CTCAE (Patient-Reported Outcomes Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) scale.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric PRO-CTCAE grade for fatigue, typically represented as an integer from 0 (none) to 4 (very severe).
definition.missing_value_rule: If no PRO-CTCAE fatigue grade is explicitly documented, the value should be represented as null.
definition.name: cancer_related_fatigue_severity

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
